collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: The wind blows away a villager's careful list of reasons to build a second room: make the list again, or let it go.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (name1) has spent all morning scratching a list onto a big leaf: every reason to build a second room on (his/her) hut, and every reason not to. It's a very good list. It's thorough. (He/she) is just reading it over one last time on the beach when a gust of wind snatches it out of (his/her) hands and carries it out to sea.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (name1) sits down and starts again from memory. (He/she) remembers most of it. Strangely, the second list is shorter. Some of the reasons just don't seem worth writing twice. When (he/she) reads it over, (he/she) realizes the "build" side is the only one (he/she) remembered clearly. (He/she) builds the second room.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (name1) watches the leaf disappear over the waves. Then (he/she) laughs. "Fine," (he/she) tells the sea. "You decide." The sea doesn't. (name1) goes home and doesn't build anything for a while. Some decisions, it turns out, are happy to wait.
